title: When detecting a limited/non-existent connectivity situation, check for restored connectivity more quickly
line: After a brief network hiccup, the "limited connectivity" warning now goes away within 30 seconds instead of staying until NetworkManager's next check minutes later.
explanation: plasma-nm's kded module asks NetworkManager for a connectivity check only once, at startup; after that it waits for NetworkManager's own periodic checks, which back off to every 5 minutes. So if one check happened during a short slow moment on a weak Wi-Fi link, the tray icon, tooltip and notification kept saying "limited connectivity" for minutes although the connection was working again. The connectivity monitor now runs a 30-second timer while connectivity is Limited that asks NetworkManager to check again, and stops it as soon as the state changes; the result arrives through NetworkManager's normal change signal, so the "Limited Connectivity" notification isn't shown again on every re-check.

commits.message:
kded: re-check connectivity every 30 seconds while it is limited

A connectivity check made during a brief slow moment kept the network
marked as limited until NetworkManager's next periodic check, minutes
later. Now we ask it to check again every 30 seconds until that clears.

BUG: 501287

media.caption: Pure master: a connectivity check during a slow moment marks the wired connection as limited (notification and tooltip).
45 seconds later the network works again, but nothing re-checks: still "limited connectivity".
With the fix: same hiccup, same limited warning at first.
The re-check 30 seconds later sees the network is fine and the warning is gone.

reviews.text: Re-checking connectivity in plasma-nm's ConnectivityMonitor when NetworkManager reports Limited is the right layer and avoids re-sending the notification by letting NetworkManager's connectivityChanged signal drive updates. However, polling NetworkManager::checkConnectivity() on an unbounded 30-second repeating timer forever will drain battery on laptops connected to local-only/offline networks and amplify load on networkcheck.kde.org by 10x during server slowdowns or outages. Firing a repeating timer without waiting for the previous D-Bus check to complete can also overlap requests on slow links.
changes: Replace the unbounded flat 30-second repeating timer with exponential backoff (e.g. 15s -> 30s -> 60s -> 120s) and stop re-checking once the interval approaches NetworkManager's own periodic check interval, resetting the backoff when connectivity leaves Limited.
Use a single-shot timer restarted only after the asynchronous NetworkManager::checkConnectivity() call finishes (via QCoro or QDBusPendingCallWatcher) so slow or timing-out checks cannot overlap.

reviews.text: This is exactly the UX change Nate proposed in comment 13: kded only asked NetworkManager for a check at startup, so a Limited result from a slow moment stuck until NM's own backed-off check; a 30 s repeating CheckConnectivity while Limited, stopped on any other state, fixes that in the right place (plasma-nm can only nudge NM's interval). The code is minimal and safe (member QTimer, capture-less lambda, async call whose result arrives through NM's normal Connectivity change signal so the notification isn't re-sent), and the dbusmock rig shows the stale warning before and its clearing at the 30 s re-check after, including the truly-limited case. Leaving None/Portal to NM is right, since None means no route/IP and NM re-checks on link changes anyway; a possible nitpick is that a permanently Limited network now gets a check every 30 s with no backoff.
